verification_report.summary: The full supplemental proof is correct under the explicitly supplied Bedford–Taylor, Gauduchon trace, and damped_measures_01 inputs, without assuming bounded mass. The uniform first local Hessian integral lets the nested-cutoff recursion stop at degree one, yielding M_j(v) <= C_j(1+A)^max(j-1,0). For the global cancellation, write H=ddc(v+q), Q=ddc q and S_m=(H-Q)^m by local expansion. All expansion factors are closed. The allowed canonical multiplication and local recursion give ddc(v S_(m-1))=S_m; correction independence makes this a global identity. Thus integral_X(ddc v)^n=0, and the binomial identity together with positivity bounds M_n by lower mixed masses, proving the range exponent r=max(n-2,0). This includes r=0 in dimensions one and two. Applying the supplied exponential transform with range n/p gives C(1+p^-1)^r with a constant independent of p and u. Choosing p=(1+t)^-1 proves shallow mass C(1+t)^r. Tonelli gives uniform polynomial mass and the tail C q/(q-r)(1+T)^(r-q) for every q>r; the level s=0 and the null pole set are handled correctly. The exponential capacity estimate retains its power n. Balancing its shallow contribution C(1+T)^n delta against the polynomial tail gives capacity exponent (q-r)/(q+n-r), with delta=0 and delta>1 treated correctly. For n>=2 this equals 1-n/(q+2); the stated coarse comparison q>n and 1-n/q is also correct. For continuity, bounded truncations and their continuous coefficients converge in capacity, and the uniform exponential and polynomial tails remove the cutoff. The GL22 attribution matches the definitions and proofs of Proposition 3.3(i) and (vi) in [Guedj–Lu (2022)](https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2022-6/2022-6-021.pdf). No critical errors or gaps were found; no novelty or optimality claim is needed.
